about: workflow:keep-commercial-events-once: keep each commercial event (a contract shared, an offer viewed, a payment made) once by its id in the person's own store, refuse an id kept again with different facts, and show one funnel's events oldest first, from the store's own keys, rules and indexes. It replaces tools/price-and-sell-by-contract/src/commercial-events.mjs, whose whole job was keeping these events in the retired record store (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep commercial events once
payload.job: Keep each commercial event once by its id in the person's own store, refuse the same id with different facts, and show one funnel's events oldest first, from the store's own objects.
payload.produces: The store's own objects for commercial events, proven on the example attempts, and each new event kept or refused and read back.

source.from: the owner, 2026-11-18 about 10:57 and 11:01 AM CST: a tool whose whole job is keeping records is a shortcut of what an AI does anyway
source.note: No tool keeps or reads the events: the run speaks to the person's store in its own language, and the store's own keys, checks and indexes hold the rules the intent below states. A funnel graph reads the store's funnel view; a trigger rule on the person's store reacts to a new event as it did to the old record.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the events are kept, when they already are

events.description: Events to keep this run, each as the intent below describes one

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where commercial events are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep and show them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form, so that the store itself refuses what the intent refuses wherever it can (keys, checks, triggers), with an index for reading one funnel's events. Grant only what the store's holder allows the person's login. Kept: Each commercial event, kept once by its event_id (up to 240 characters, no slash): what happened (event), who or what it is about (subject_kind and subject_id), and when (occurred_at, a date and time). Optional: the funnel it feeds (funnel_id) and the stage there (stage), whether it converted (converted, true or false), an amount (amount_cents, a whole number not below zero) and its currency (three capital letters, such as USD). Any other fact the caller gives is kept too when its name is lowercase letters, digits and underscores (starting with a letter, up to 64) and its value is text up to 2000 characters, a number or true/false. Keeping: Keeping an event whose event_id is already kept, with the same facts, changes nothing (it is a repeat). A repeat that gives no occurred_at keeps the first one's time, and its other facts must still match. Keeping an event whose event_id is already kept with any different fact is refused, and the first is kept unchanged. An event that breaks a rule above is refused and nothing is kept. Shown: The events of one funnel, oldest first; events at the same time in event_id order. The events whose facts match a rule (for example event equals negotiated_offer_paid), oldest first. Who may: Only the person (and whoever they allow) reads or keeps events. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Keep this run's events
steps.do: Keep each item of events through the store's own objects, in order, and read every kept id back. Submit kept_ids (kept or repeated), refused (each refused event's id and the store's own words for why) and found_ids. With no events, submit three empty lists.
